conceptZh: 風會吹動東西，我們看不見它
object: a wind-up animal band with a bunny, a bear and a duck, plus a kite
morph: two band halves pull a streamer in opposite directions until strokes spring together into 風
creativeAngle: 發條樂團兩邊拉布條，風一吹就把風箏、筆畫吹成字。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 風 (wind). Lead: a wind-up band of a bunny with cymbals, a bear with a drum and a duck with a horn, keys turning on their backs. Moment 1 (0-1.7s): the band tries to start, the horn honks and a gust blows the drummer sideways; the voice says 風. Moment 2 (1.7-3.4s): bunny and bear tug a long ribbon in opposite directions; the gust blows the ribbon into 風 on the second 風, the strokes snapping like elastic. Moment 3 (3.4-5.3s): the ribbon becomes the tail of a red diamond kite that lifts the duck; as the voice says 風箏 the kite loops high and the band waves from below. Moment 4 (5.3-8s): glyph still; the bear sways with the wind, drum rolling silently. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "風、風、風箏" (ㄈㄥ、ㄈㄥ、ㄈㄥ ㄓㄥ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 風, drawn as saturated solid teal blue strokes on a pale warm cream background, correctly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.

conceptZh: 浣熊助手花生抱著一疊高到搖晃的積木小隊敬錯禮，一陣大風把他吹得像皮球一樣在地板、牆壁、天花板間彈來彈去，每彈一下就「喀」地撞出風字的一筆，最後一撞把積木小隊撞倒成裡面的「虫」，花生暈呼呼地坐在風字頂上，風再把他的紅圍巾吹成一隻風箏。
object: a wobbling tower of teal building bricks carried by Peanut the cartoon raccoon, and one swirling visible gust of wind
morph: the gust knocks Peanut into a wild bounce chain; each ricochet off floor, wall and ceiling clacks a run of bricks into one stroke of 風 (the left sweeping stroke, the tall right hook, the short inner horizontal), and the final bonk topples the brick squad into the 虫 shape inside, finishing the glyph with Peanut seated on top
creativeAngle: 前一版是三隻動物樂隊拉緞帶的靜態變形，這版改成完全不同的「彈跳連鎖」肢體喜劇：花生本人就是那顆被風吹飛的皮球，每一次彈跳都看得到、聽得到地敲出一筆，積木小隊在最糟的時刻倒下剛好補成「虫」，讓六歲孩子能一眼讀懂「風吹→亂彈→字完成」的因果。風箏從花生的紅圍巾變出來，說「風箏」時畫面上正好有風箏升起，聲音與畫面同步。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright 2D-style animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 風 (wind). Pale warm cream background, nothing busy behind. Lead: Peanut, an original cartoon raccoon sidekick with a striped tail, a tiny red scarf and a too-big cap, who always balances a wobbling tower of things far too tall for him and salutes at the wrong moment. Supporting prop: a squad of chunky interlocking teal building bricks with little dot eyes that march, stack and topple at the worst possible moment.

Moment 1 (0 to 1.5s): Peanut stands at left, proudly balancing a swaying tower of teal bricks on one paw, saluting crisply with the other. He stares at the tower, wants it to stay up. From the left edge a big swirling gust of wind rolls in, drawn as curling pale blue swirl lines with two flying leaves. As the voice says 風 the gust hits; the tower bends like a noodle and Peanut's cap flips.

Moment 2 (1.5 to 3.5s): The gust lifts Peanut off his feet and he bounces like a rubber ball, squash and stretch, grinning in panic. BOING off the floor: a run of bricks clacks into the left curving sweep of 風. BOING off the right wall: more bricks clack into the tall right-hand stroke that curves down and ends in an upward hook. BOING off the ceiling: a short row of bricks drops in as the small horizontal bar near the top inside the frame. The voice says the second 風 as these strokes snap into place with crisp clacks.

Moment 3 (3.5 to 5s): The brick squad, still marching in a neat column, salutes back at Peanut at exactly the wrong moment. Peanut's last big bounce BONKS off the squad leader's head; the whole squad topples forward inside the frame and lands as the 虫 shape, a small box on top with the vertical and the hooked base stroke and the final dot. Peanut rebounds once more and plops down seated on the very top of the finished 風, cap spinning, eyes going in little circles, dizzy happy grin.

Moment 4 (5 to 8s): The glyph 風 is complete, perfectly still and readable: saturated solid teal strokes, correctly formed standard Traditional shape, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with clear margins. The gust gives one last puff and Peanut's red scarf stretches up into a small red diamond kite with a wiggly tail, floating in the upper right corner away from the strokes; exactly as the kite lifts, the voice says 風箏. Peanut holds its string in one paw and gives a wobbly salute with the other, swaying slightly on top of the glyph without covering any stroke.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly 風、風、風箏 (ㄈㄥ、ㄈㄥ、ㄈㄥ ㄓㄥ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, one utterance per moment as described, then stops; no other speech, no English, no music louder than the voice; gentle cartoon boing and clack sounds only, nothing loud or startling. The only on-screen text is the single glyph 風; no vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, logos, clutter or flashing. Stylized cartoon characters and objects only, no real people or realistic humans. Bright but not neon, no white blowouts, no dark grading.
